flags.sentence: Fiction reading time was not significantly correlated with the three variants of the RMET score: r(378) = .003, .006, and .006 for the RMET-A, RMET-B, and total RMET (i.e., RMET-A + RMET-B) scores, respectively (all ps > .40).
flags.explanation: 'all ps > .40' is a blanket p statement covering several tests at once. It cannot be checked against a specific test statistic.

flags.sentence: In fact, the correlation between RMET-A and RMET-B was low: r(402) = .30.
flags.explanation: 'r(402) = .30' is reported without a p value in the same sentence, so it cannot be verified. The statistic implies a two-tailed p = 7.58e-10.

flags.sentence: Moreover, RMET performance is known to be positively associated with vocabulary (our measure of vocabulary was also significantly, but weakly, correlated with RMET score: r402 = .098, p = .049).
flags.explanation: 'p = .049' is a p value without a test statistic in the same sentence, so it cannot be recomputed.

disclaimer: This report lists places where a value reported in the paper differs from the value recomputed from other reported numbers. A difference is not evidence of misconduct. Common benign causes are rounding, typos, one-tailed tests, corrections for multiple comparisons, adjusted degrees of freedom, non-integer scales (which make GRIM and GRIMMER inapplicable) and PDF text-extraction errors. Each flag should be read in the paper before drawing any conclusion.
